correctness.rationale: For every positive m,k, validity of \(\Box^{m+k}p\to\Box^mp\) on F is equivalent to \(R^m\subseteq R^{m+k}\): choose p true on the longer-step reachable set to witness failure. A repeated-vertex segment of length ell<=n can be inserted \(k/\ell\) times whenever ell divides \(L_n\) and \(L_n\) divides k. This establishes the unrestricted upper criterion \(m\ge n\). In a serial n-world frame, a non-repeating walk of length n-1 visits all worlds, and seriality supplies an outgoing terminal edge returning to the visited path, giving a terminal closed walk of length 1..n and the exact serial one-step improvement. Simple directed paths, serial paths with a terminal loop, and directed cycles of lengths not dividing k give sharp failures; these also prove minimum frame cardinalities. The actual adjacent verify.cpp was compiled with C++17 and executed, producing VERIFY_OK for all 66066 labeled frames through four vertices, 50978 serial frames, and 4756752 graph/parameter cases. No finite sample replaces the all-parameter combinatorial proof. All domains and empty-successor semantics are explicit.

originality.rationale: Knudstorp (arXiv:2510.00864, later JSL) proves FMP of the modal logic obtained by imposing reduction axioms, not the exact minimum n of a finite frame violating a chosen axiom, with distinct n for serial and unrestricted semantics. The 1999 Boolean-matrix power preprint treats eventual periodicity and powers; the modern Euler–Fermat equality reported in arXiv:2607.09677 holds only after a quadratic exponent, and neither directly implies the sharp one-sided insertion threshold at n, or its serial n-1 variant. Exact queries for aliases, relation-power inclusion, minimal counterframes, deterministic transition frames and Boolean-matrix powers produced no matching claim among retrieved results; this is evidence of limited coverage rather than proof of novelty. Substantial residual overlap risk remains because elementary cycle-insertion bounds or semigroup inclusions could have been separately described in older sources.
residual_risks: Cycle-pumping facts are elementary; older finite-automata or Boolean-semigroup literature might have given exactly the same early one-sided bounds in a different notation.
A source identifying the full serial/unrestricted threshold pair under a less obvious equivalence would defeat originality; searches and inspected sources are not exhaustive.
The motivating article addresses a different finite model property, so the present least-invalidating-frame invariant should not be presented as its direct generalization or an FMP improvement.

value.rationale: The full natural two-parameter family of modal reduction axioms now has exact smallest finite counterframe orders over both K and KD frames, with deterministic optimal witnesses. The seriality boundary has a sharp and genuinely structural one-world phase transition determined by divisibility of k by lcm(1,...,m+1); the looped-tail and cycle obstructions play provably distinct roles. For fixed m this yields infinitely many strict gaps and exact size thresholds for exhaustive axiom-testing algorithms. This is a natural complete finite invariant and not an arbitrary numeric slice. The result does not claim FMP for general formulas or a paper-sized theory, and derives value from a nontrivial exact structural cutoff beyond the correctness of enumeration.
